newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to tell G7 overly weak yen unfavourable--MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan to tell G7 overly weak yen unfavourable--MOF.

text.p: Japan's Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Friday that Japan will exchange views with Group of Seven nations based on a stance that excessive weakness or strength in the yen is unfavourable.
He added that the G7 nations will exchange views on economic and fiscal matters and work towards stabilising economies.
"We will exchange views based on our stance that excessive weakness in the yen as well as excessive strength in the yen is unfavourable," Mitsuzuka said.
He added that he believed that the G7 nations agree that stable foreign exchange markets are important for each economy.

Asked whether he was planning any bilateral talks at Saturday's G7 meeting in Berlin, Mitsuzuka said that he would meet the German finance minister and was in the process of scheduling a meeting with U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin.
Mitsuzuka added that monetary authorities of G7 nations were maintaining cooperative ties on foreign exchange.
